summary: [¶] Petition under Section 79 (1) (c) & (k) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 42 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the Inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022 seeking directions and/or guidelines for the implementation of Regulation 11A and Regulation 24.6, concerning nature and treatment of extensions or delayed commissioning by Renewable Energy Implementing Agencies (REIAs) or Distributions Licensees. [¶] The Petitioner, Central Transmission Utility of India Limited (‘CTUIL’), has filed the present Petition seeking necessary directions and/or guidelines in regard to the nature and treatment of extensions by Renewable Energy Implementation Agencies (REIAs) or distribution licensees for the purposes of compliance with Regulation 11A and Regulation 24 of the GNA Regulations, 2022. [para 2] 2. The Petitioner has filed the present Petition seeking the following relief(s): [para 3] 3. The matter was heard on 3.6.2026. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition has been filed seeking necessary directions and/or guidelines in regard to the nature and treatment of extensions by Renewable Energy Implementation Agencies (REIAs) or distribution licensees for the purposes of compliance with Regulation 11A and Regulation 24 of the GNA Regulations. The learned counsel, while pointing out one such extension granted by [para 4] 4. The matter was mentioned by the learned counsel for the Petitioner on 11.6.2026 and apprised that the Respondent, APIPL, is pursuing a separate Petition [¶] (Diary) No. 388/2026 along with IA (Diary) No. 389/2026, seeking quashing of the revocation of APIPL’s connectivity and other reliefs. Therefore, in terms of the order dated 31.5.2026 in Petition No. 1015/MP/2025 (Datta Power Infra Private Limited v CTUIL), nothing survives in the instant Petition. The learned counsel for the Petitioner sought permission to withdraw the instant Petition. The learned counsel for the Respondent, APIPL, did not oppose the Petitioner’s request for withdrawal of the Petition. [para 5] 5. Considering the submissions of the learned counsels for the parties, the Petitioner is permitted to withdraw the present Petition. [para 6] 6. Petition No. 259/MP/2026 is disposed of as withdrawn.
